taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes the name A. velox was applied to triploid parthenogens by Wright (1993) while the diploid A. innotata is treated as a separate species; older references use Cnemidophorus velox.
fieldMarks: Long, slender lizard with dark and light stripes running the length of the body.
Adults reach about 8.7 cm snout-vent (28 cm total length).
Hatchlings (33-37 mm snout-vent) have a bright blue tail.
All individuals are female; the species reproduces by parthenogenesis.
behavior: Diurnal; usually active from May to September (hatchlings may be active into mid-October).
Reproduces without males: clutches of 3-5 eggs are laid late June to early July and hatchlings emerge from mid-August.
habitat: Pinyon-juniper woodland, mountain shrubland, sagebrush, open chaparral, oak woodland and riparian areas, and lower elevations of ponderosa pine and Douglas-fir forest.
range: Colorado Plateau and vicinity in southern Utah, western Colorado, northern Arizona and northern New Mexico at about 1,200-2,440 m; introduced and established at Cove Palisades State Park, Oregon.
